newsitem.title: USA: British Airways rejects mediation - attny.
newsitem.headline: British Airways rejects mediation - attny.

text.p: British Airways Plc has declined the Florida attorney general's offer to mediate in an antitrust lawsuit filed against the carrier by Laker Airways Inc, a spokesman for Attorney General Bob Butterworth said Friday.
British Airways said in a letter to Butterworth that it believed Laker's lawsuit was groundless and that there was "no real issue to be mediated."

British Airways offered to meet with the attorney general's staff to explain its position. The meeting is tentatively set for July 15 in the office of Miami attorney Parker Thomson, whom Butterworth had proposed as the mediator.

Florida-based Laker Airways sued British Airways in U.S. District Court in Miami in June, alleging British Airways used its dominant position to prevent Laker from getting desirable takeoff and landing slots at London's Gatwick Airport.

The lawsuit said British Airways's alleged actions forced Laker's London-to-Miami flights to land after connecting flights to Central and South America and the Caribbean had all gone, depriving the carrier of potential business.

Butterworth offered to mediate on grounds that the allegations could affect Florida's economically important tourism industry. Laker accepted the offer but British Airways declined, Butterworth spokesman Joe Bizzaro said.

"We think there is no substance to the claims made by Laker Airways and are advised that the Laker complaint does not state any claim under the antitrust laws either of the United States or of the State of Florida," British Airways's attorney wrote in a reply to Butterworth.
British Airways said it would file a request next week to dismiss the lawsuit.
